description: WALRUS historical state engine, driven by walrussim.

panels.description: The read amplification the schema pays for never compacting. This is the number the project exists to measure.
panels.title: Pods Probed (p99)

panels.description: Answers that disagreed with the workload's own model. Must be zero.
panels.title: Mismatches

panels.description: The window Get can answer for. The floor rises as retention collects; the ceiling trails the newest appended block by a pod and a build.
panels.title: Queryable Block Range

panels.description: Where the writer loop's wall clock goes. committing is the state stub, which is pebble standing in for FlatKV and measures nothing about WALRUS. appending is the engine. waiting_for_blocks is the workload generator failing to keep up.
panels.title: Time Spent

panels.description: Seconds per second in each phase. These sum to about 1.0; whichever phase owns most of it is the bottleneck.
panels.title: Time Spent

panels.description: The same split divided by block rate, so it reads as seconds of each phase per block regardless of how fast the run is going.
panels.title: Time Spent Per Block (amortized)

panels.description: How long a single visit to each phase takes. A high snapshotting p99 against a low total means checkpoints are rare but stall the writer.
panels.title: Phase Latency (p99)

panels.description: The gap between the two is real accumulator work. If they converge, pod building is the write path's limit.
panels.title: Append Time and Build Backpressure

panels.description: What actually reaches disk, split across a pod's three files. The index is the bulk of the schema's overhead; the bloom filter is noise.
panels.title: Bytes / Second Written, by File

panels.description: Bytes written to disk per byte of key change appended. A pure append log would be 1.0; the excess is index and filter.
panels.title: Write Amplification

panels.description: Seconds per second that appends spent waiting for a build slot. 1.0 means the write path is entirely blocked on pod building.
panels.title: Append Backpressure

panels.description: Pods submitted but not yet built. Sitting at the configured concurrency means builds are the bottleneck.
panels.title: Build Queue Depth

panels.description: The two sides of the same handoff, counted independently. They should sit on top of each other; a gap means blocks or changes are being lost between the harness and the engine.
panels.title: Appends Counted by Engine and Harness

panels.description: Time to write one pod's data file, index, and bloom filter.
panels.title: Pod Build Latency

panels.description: Entries counts every version of every key; keys counts them once. Their ratio is how much rewriting the workload does.
panels.title: Pod Shape

panels.description: Time inside the engine to answer one historical read.
panels.title: Read Latency

panels.description: missing is a read with nothing to find at or below the queried block: it walks every pod and then the floor snapshot, so it is the engine's worst case. present stops as soon as the walk reaches the key.
panels.title: Read Latency by Key Presence

panels.description: What the workload is actually asking for, which sets how much of the latency distribution comes from the worst case.
panels.title: Reads / Second by Key Presence

panels.description: Measured by the harness. never_written keys walk to the floor every time, so they are the tail; averaging them with live keys hides both.
panels.title: Read Latency by Key Class

panels.description: Where a read's time goes: bloom is ruling pods out, index is searching the pods that were not ruled out, data is reading the located entry, snapshot is the floor read a walk that found nothing falls back to.
panels.title: Read Time by Phase (average)

panels.description: Bloom filters tested to answer one query. Bounded by the snapshot interval: a walk stops at the newest snapshot at or below the queried block.
panels.title: Pods Probed per Query

panels.description: Pods probed converted to blocks, which is comparable across configurations with different pod sizes.
panels.title: Blocks Probed per Query (p99)

panels.description: ruled_out is the filter working. true_positive is a pod that really held the key. false_positive is an index search done for nothing.
panels.title: Bloom Filter Outcomes

panels.description: False positives over the pods that did not hold the key, which is the textbook definition. Should track the configured rate.
panels.title: Bloom False Positive Rate

panels.description: The gap is what the bloom filters saved. Searched is what cost an index lookup.
panels.title: Pods Probed and Searched

panels.description: What the retention window is holding on disk.
panels.title: Retained Bytes

panels.description: The space cost of making the log searchable, as a fraction of the log.
panels.title: Index Overhead

panels.description: Retention deleting what has fallen below the floor.
panels.title: Collection

panels.description: Policy raises the query floor; the floor block only advances onto a real snapshot. A persistent gap means retention is waiting for one.
panels.title: Retention Floors

panels.description: Admitted queries holding references. Collection cannot delete what these are reading.
panels.title: Queries In Flight

panels.description: Checkpoints produced by the state stub and retained by the engine.
panels.title: Snapshots / Second

panels.description: Checkpointing the state stub and hard-linking it. This stalls the write path, so at a short snapshot interval it is a real share of wall clock.
panels.title: Snapshot Duration

title: WALRUS
